title: Pioneering Protein Degradation for Agricultural Applications
projectDescription: Global proteomics analysis of Sf9 cells treated with Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) designed to engage fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) sfBRD3 or sfWDS and to recruit the insect VHL (von Hippel-Lindau) E3 ligase.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Sf9 protein was extracted using a 20mM Tris pH7.8, 1%SDS buffer containing 1x HALT protease (Pierce). The protein extract was diluted in half with equal volume of 20 mM Tris pH 7.8 150 mM NaCl 5 mM MgCl2 containing 1:10,000 Benzonase (Promega). Approximately 50 mg total protein was transferred to assay plate for acetone precipitation. The pellets were solubilized with 8M urea containing 50 mM DTT then alkylated with iodoacetamide and digested with Trypsin/Lys-C (Promega) 1:50 overnight 37C. The resulting peptides were desalted and cleaned by Oasis MCX (Waters) then dried in a speed vac. The peptide samples were solubilized in 0.1% formic acid (100 mL) 0.5ug, (n=5-6) were analyzed using a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral Mass Spectrometer coupled to a Vanquish Neo UHPLC system. Tryptic peptides were separated on a 15cm C18 analytical column (Thermo Scientific ES75150PN) using a linear gradient of 2–40% acetonitrile in 0.1% formic acid over 20 minutes at a flow rate of 0.35 µL/min.
dataProcessingProtocol: Data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode was set as follows: MS1 resolution 240,000 across an m/z range of 380–980, with an AGC target of 500% and a maximum injection time of 5 ms. MS/MS spectra collected across 299 staggered isolation windows (2 m/z width), covering an m/z range of 150–2000, at a resolution of 30,000. Raw data files were acquired using Xcalibur™ v1.7 (Thermo Scientific) and analyzed using DIANN v1.8 (Vadim Demichev Laboratory) with a curated Spodoptera frugiperda proteome database, followed by Direct LFQ (Mann Labs) for label-free quantification, finally, statistical results analysis was performed in Perseus (Cox Lab).
